people/altshiller-court.title: Nathan Altshiller-Court
people/altshiller-court.description: Author of College Geometry: An Introduction to the Modern Geometry of the Triangle and the Circle, heavily referenced in Seelig’s harmonic and similitude derivations.

people/apollonius.title: Apollonius
people/apollonius.description: Greek geometer known as ‘The Great Geometer’, author of Conics and discoverer of the Apollonian circles of constant distance ratio.

people/carnot.title: Carnot
people/carnot.description: French mathematician and engineer whose Géométrie de position (1803) introduced signed geometric quantities and Carnot’s theorem.

people/ceva.title: Ceva
people/ceva.description: Italian mathematician who published De lineis rectis (1678), establishing Ceva’s theorem for concurrent cevians in a triangle.

people/conway.title: Conway
people/conway.description: English mathematician who introduced Conway triangle notation (S, S_A, S_B, S_C, S_omega), extensively adopted by Fred Seelig throughout his notebooks.

people/coxeter.title: Coxeter
people/coxeter.description: Geometer and co-author of Geometry Revisited, frequently cited in the notebooks for coaxial circles, inversion, and projective geometry.

people/dalembert.title: Dalembert
people/dalembert.description: French mathematician and physicist associated with d’Alembert’s theorem on the collinearity of external and internal centers of similitude of three circles (Monge–d’Alembert theorem).

people/dorrie.title: Dorrie
people/dorrie.description: German mathematician and author of 100 Great Problems of Elementary Mathematics, cited by Seelig in his study of the Problem of Apollonius.

people/euclid.title: Euclid
people/euclid.description: Greek mathematician and author of the Elements, whose compass-and-straightedge propositions underpin the constructive foundations of every topic in this codex.

people/euler.title: Euler
people/euler.description: Swiss mathematician who proved the collinearity of the orthocenter, centroid, nine-point center, and circumcenter (the Euler line) and the distance formula d^2 = R(R - 2r) between incenter and circumc

people/fagnano.title: Fagnano
people/fagnano.description: Italian mathematician who proved in 1775 that the orthic triangle minimizes perimeter among all triangles inscribed in an acute triangle.

people/fermat.title: Fermat
people/fermat.description: French mathematician who posed the problem of finding the point minimizing the sum of distances to the three vertices of a triangle.

people/feuerbach.title: Feuerbach
people/feuerbach.description: German geometer who proved in 1822 that the nine-point circle is internally tangent to the incircle and externally tangent to the three excircles.

people/heron.title: Heron
people/heron.description: Greek mathematician and engineer who gave the classical proof of Heron’s formula for the area of a triangle in terms of its side lengths.

people/kimberling.title: Kimberling
people/kimberling.description: American mathematician and creator of the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers (ETC), whose X(n) indexing links directly to Seelig’s triangle studies.

people/markowski.title: Markowski
people/markowski.description: Mathematician examined in Seelig’s Topic 32 notebook for the circumcircle midpoint-sagitta theorem JKL = (1/2)r^2R = (R^2 - d_IO^2)^2 / (8R).

people/menelaus.title: Menelaus
people/menelaus.description: Greek mathematician and astronomer who formulated Menelaus’s theorem for collinearity on a triangle’s sidelines.

people/newton.title: Newton
people/newton.description: English mathematician and physicist whose Universal Arithmetick established algebraic triangle relations such as c = s - K/s for right triangles.

people/ogilvy.title: Ogilvy
people/ogilvy.description: American mathematician and author of Excursions in Geometry (1969), frequently cited by Fred Seelig for coaxial circles, harmonic division, and orthogonal circle inversion.

people/pappus.title: Pappus
people/pappus.description: Hellenistic mathematician whose Synagoge (Collection) preserved projective invariants, harmonic cross-ratios, and Stewart’s theorem precursors.

people/phi.title: Phi
people/phi.description: Founder and principal investigator of the GEOMETOR Project, standardizing synthetic constructive geometry into executable Python models, interactive theme-adaptive SVG plates, and multi-track Book Cod

people/plato.title: Plato
people/plato.description: Founder of the Academy in Athens above whose gates stood the inscription Let no one ignorant of geometry enter here. Formulated the cosmological role of regular polyhedra in Timaeus.

people/poncelet.title: Poncelet
people/poncelet.description: French mathematician and founder of modern projective geometry, developing pole-polar duality, harmonic ranges, and coaxial pencils.

people/ptolemy.title: Ptolemy
people/ptolemy.description: Alexandrian astronomer and mathematician whose Almagest established Ptolemy’s theorem on the diagonals and sides of a cyclic quadrilateral.

people/pythagoras.title: Pythagoras
people/pythagoras.description: Ionian philosopher and mathematician whose brotherhood established number as the essence of reality and discovered the incommensurability of the diagonal and the foundational theorem of right-angled t

people/seelig.title: Seelig
people/seelig.description: Independent geometric researcher and compiler of the 55 notebooks and computational spreadsheets forming the GEOMETOR Fundamentals archive. His investigations bridge classical synthetic geometry, Conw

people/steiner.title: Steiner
people/steiner.description: Swiss geometer who systematized the power of a point, radical axes, and synthetic projective constructions.

people/stewart.title: Stewart
people/stewart.description: Scottish mathematician who published Stewart’s theorem in Some General Theorems of Considerable Use in the Higher Parts of Mathematics (1746).

people/torricelli.title: Torricelli
people/torricelli.description: Italian physicist and mathematician who gave the classical equilateral-triangle circumcircle construction for the Fermat–Torricelli point X(13).

people/yiu.title: Yiu
people/yiu.description: Mathematician and author of Introduction to the Geometry of the Triangle, a primary reference in Fred Seelig’s notes on homogeneous barycentric coordinates.
